title: Abu Hassan al-Ziyadi
summary: Abu Hassan al-Ziyadi was an eminent scholar and judge of Baghdad in the reign of the Caliph Al-Ma'mun. Known for his profound learning in jurisprudence and his generosity to stu...
full_text:
Abu Hassan al-Ziyadi was an eminent scholar and judge of Baghdad in the reign of the Caliph Al-Ma'mun. Known for his profound learning in jurisprudence and his generosity to students, he was also burdened by heavy debts, having borrowed money to support poor scholars who flocked to his lectures.

A day arrived when his creditors gathered before his gate, demanding payment of ten thousand dinars. Abu Hassan had not a single dirham in his house, and his larder was completely bare. He spent the entire day praying for deliverance and reflecting on his duties.

That night, as he sat in the dark reading by the light of a tiny oil wick, a knocking sounded at his door. A messenger from the imperial palace entered, saying: 'The Commander of the Faithful summons you immediately!'

Abu Hassan dressed in his patched cloak, believing that his creditors had complained to the Caliph and that imprisonment awaited him.

When he entered the imperial audience hall, Caliph Al-Ma'mun stepped down from his dais, took the scholar by the hand, and said: 'Peace be upon you, Abu Hassan! Know that tonight, as I slept, a vision appeared to me three times, commanding: "Deliver Abu Hassan al-Ziyadi from his affliction, for his prayers have reached the heavens!" Tell me, what distress has befallen you?'

Abu Hassan, with tears in his eyes, recounted the debts he had incurred to feed his poor scholars and sustain his academy of learning.

The Caliph embraced him with deep reverence, ordered thirty thousand gold dinars to be delivered to his home—ten thousand to pay his debts, ten thousand to expand his academy, and ten thousand for his household—and appointed him the Chief Justice of the eastern provinces.

Abu Hassan returned home at dawn, marveling at how sincere devotion and selfless dedication to truth are answered in the hour of greatest need.
moral: Trust in providence, faithful adherence to duty, and generous patience will turn the darkest midnight into a radiant dawn.
